item.title: Trump rules out diesel export ban after Europe agrees to tap reserves
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Friday he was ruling out a diesel export ban and never really considered one in the first place, hours after Europe caved to U.S. pressure and agreed to release fuel from its stockpiles.

The announcement appears to put to rest more than a week of frantic lobbying across two continents after surging fuel prices — caused by the ongoing war against Iran as well as Ukrainian attacks against Russian refineries — have angered farmers and put pressure on the Trump administration to act ahead of the November midterm elections.

"Europe has a lot of diesel, and they're going to be making a major world contribution, and so are we," Trump told reporters as he left the White House for a campaign trip. "And we're not going to be doing the export ban.

"It was never really ever on the table, but what Europe did was a great thing," he added.

Trump had repeatedly said over the last two weeks that he was open to suspending exports of the fuel, which would have been the first restriction on U.S. energy exports since the Obama administration lifted a decades-old ban on oil exports in 2015. The president said just over a week ago that "I've called for that" when asked about a possible ban.

But Energy Secretary Chris Wright and the president's allies in the oil industry publicly condemned the idea, warning it could pose major economic problems for foreign countries who rely on U.S. imports and eventually result in higher pump prices at home as refiners scaled back production.

Those advisers urged Trump instead to push Europe to release fuel from its stockpiles, prompting a frantic public and private campaign of European governments by Trump administration officials. The G-7 announced Friday morning they would release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from their strategic reserves over the next four months, beginning with a "frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days."

POLITICO reported earlier Friday that the U.S. had essentially strong-armed hesitant EU governments into releasing their diesel supplies with the threat of an export ban, with one European diplomat labeling it "blackmail."

Trump told reporters Friday that he had "asked for" Europe to tap its stockpiles, but maintained that the Europeans had decided to tap their stockpiles out of their own volition.

"We have a very good relationship with Europe, and they wanted to do it because they have a lot of diesel," Trump said. "I said it would be great if you put it out to the markets, and they did it."

The Trump administration could still announce further measures on diesel prices short of a ban next week, according to two people familiar with the discussions. Among the ideas being evaluated are pushing more states to lift restrictions on red-dyed off-road diesel and suspend excise taxes on diesel sales.

Meredith Lee Hill and Ben Lefebvre contributed reporting.

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/trump-rules-diesel-export-ban-213037393.html

item.title: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito confirms he's considering retirement
item.description:
Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito has confirmed that he is considering retirement, leaving open the possibility that he could leave after next year’s term and hand another nomination to President Donald Trump.

Alito said in excerpts of a CBS News interview released Friday that he thought about retiring this year and will do so again in 2027.

“It’s something that I think that somebody at my age has to think about every term,” the 76-year-old said in the interview scheduled to air Monday. “But I thought that I could still make a valuable contribution, which is why I became a justice and a judge in the first place.”

Alito’s interview, the first in a number of expected appearances to coincide with the release of a book about his judicial philosophy, raises the possibility that Trump, whose judicial picks shifted the Supreme Court to the right, may get an opportunity to nominate a fourth justice.

The president, who expressed regret in a recent interview about several nominees who ruled against his administration on some issues, would have a harder time getting a fourth pick through the Senate if Democrats win control in the midterms.

Alito, in the CBS interview, pushed back on concerns that the timing of his retirement and his replacement could potentially unravel his work on the bench.

“It’s too hard to predict what the political situation will be and what any president might do with respect to a replacement,” he said.

Alito also defended his majority opinion in June 2022 that struck down Roe v. Wade and overturned the constitutional protections for abortion that had prevailed for decades. The decision closely matched one that had leaked a month earlier.

“We didn’t know it when we produced the draft that was leaked, but it required courage to go ahead with that because of the implications,” he said.

He said the decision resulted in the loss of old friendships.

“That’s something you have to live with,” he said, adding, “It’s part of the job that you’re going to displease people by making decisions on controversial matters, because one side or the other is going to really dislike you because of the decisions.”

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/02/alito-supreme-court-retirement-01105789

item.title: 美共和党议员：美中应避免脱钩，台湾政策应维持现在路线
item.description: 美国共和党联邦参议员史蒂夫·戴恩斯(Steve Daines)表示，美国不应寻求与中国全面脱钩，而应在保持接触的同时降低风险。他强调，美国需要保持经济和军事力量，并通过外交沟通避免美中关系进一步升级。在台湾议题上，戴恩斯主张“保持现有路线”。

item.title: 外交事务：人工智能如何赋予独裁者权力，又会如何危及独裁者
item.description:
从短期来看，AI可能给威权政权带来巨大利益。 尽管技术部署仍面临很多障碍，AI已经能够提供成本更低的监控、更智能的审查系统，同时减少统治者必须担心和防范的人类下属。 但对于威权统治者来说，人工智能的诱惑最终可能让他们重新跌入自己原本想逃离的陷阱。 一个政权越依赖AI，就越依赖那些维持AI运转的人。 而这些人和历史上的每一支禁卫军一样，很快就会意识到，自己不可替代的地位究竟值多少钱。

item.title: 史无前例 中国男足主场0-5败给巴勒斯坦
item.description:
来源: 
新唐人

中共领导下的体育腐败越来越严重，中国男足被指其典型代表。近年来，国足的表现越来越差，引来骂声一片。日前又在重庆主场首次惨败给巴勒斯坦。

北京时间10月2日晚，中国男足在重庆龙兴足球场进行的CFA中国之队国际足球邀请赛中，以0比5败给巴勒斯坦队。

据大陆媒体报导，这是国足历史上首次输给巴勒斯坦队。过去67年来，两队7次交手，中国队战绩是5胜2平，总计攻入17球仅丢2球，1966年甚至7比0大胜。

10月2日的这场比赛，中国队上半场就防线崩溃，连丢三球。第16分钟，中国队后场解围失误，巴勒斯坦前锋爆射破门；第22分钟，巴勒斯坦直塞打穿防线，单刀直入再次破门，中国队6分钟内连丢2球；上半场补时第5分钟，巴勒斯坦队员禁区外远射得分。中国队上半场0比3落后，控球率不足四成。

下半场第54分钟，巴勒斯坦队员射门，中国队守门员扑救脱手；伤停补时第3分钟，巴勒斯坦替补队员远射破门，将最终比分定格为0比5。

赛后中国男足主帅邵佳一公开道歉，并称“没有什么更多的解释”，“接受一切批评， 希望打好下一场比赛”。

当天，“国足0比5败给巴勒斯坦”的消息迅速冲上大陆热搜榜。许多球迷纷纷痛斥：“还要脸吗？”

还有不少球迷留言嘲讽：“一个天天打仗流离失所的国家，都能5:0踢赢年薪百万的球队”“我来回翻了八遍，确认是巴勒斯坦没错，真不是巴基斯坦”“恭喜巴勒斯坦老铁喜提净胜球，咱们这友谊赛真是友谊到家了”“见怪不怪了”“确实没啥好意外的，这水平输谁都不奇怪”“说到底责任都在美国那边”。

关键词: 
中国男足
巴勒斯坦队
栏目: 
要闻
作者: 
陈镇锦

item.title: 外交政策：泰国人口危机提前到来
item.description:
去年9月，一批泰国学者提出，人们不愿生孩子，并不只是因为生活成本上涨，还与对生活方式的期待有关，而社交媒体可能进一步强化这种期待。 他们援引“相对收入假说”，认为“年轻人在决定是否生孩子时，并不是只看绝对收入，而是会比较自己目前的生活水平与自己预期应该达到的生活水平”。 45岁的萨里拉·查塔库尔猜住在清迈，去年刚刚结婚。她说，自己倾向于不要孩子，其中一个原因是对泰国教育体系和政治局势感到担忧。 她说：“泰国公立学校体系让我觉得已经落伍，与今天的全球标准并不接轨。” 她还说，自己曾经在澳大利亚留学，这段经历也影响了她对教育问题的看法。 泰国的公立教育和公共医疗通常免费，但顶级国际学校和私人医疗的费用可能非常高。 清迈收费最高的国际高中，每年学费约2.5万美元，大约相当于泰国人均国内生产总值的3倍。 查塔库尔猜还担忧泰国长期存在的政治不稳定。 过去25年，泰国已经更换过10名总理，其中两人在军事政变中被推翻。 她说：“这些因素都会影响长期政策的连续性，包括教育改革和经济发展。”
